newsitem.title: COMOROS: Army moves to restore order after Comoros clashes.
newsitem.headline: Army moves to restore order after Comoros clashes.

text.p: Army troops in the Comoros island of Anjouan detained hundreds of people amid allegations soldiers were torturing detainees in the battle to put down the secessionist rebellion that broke out last week.

Residents on Sunday said that more than 200 people, including a former parliamentarian, were arrested after clashes between stone-throwing villagers and armed troops on Anjouan, the largest of the Comoro Islands.
The Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies said security forces moved on Sunday to Sima, 25 km (15 miles) west of the Anjouan capital, Mutsamudu.
They said they had received numerous complaints that soldiers were assaulting and torturing people -- some of whom were stripped and forced to crawl as soldiers beat them with guns.
The sound of gunfire continued to echo over the island, where terrified civilians huddled in their homes.
Four people were killed and at least 20 wounded on Anjouan on Saturday in fighting between troops and secessionists in rebellion against the government of the Indian Ocean islands.
Local MP and Islamic fundamentalist leader Ahmed Abdullah Sambi said he was forced back when he tried to visit arrested civilians in the local gendarmerie.
Residents said the soldiers broke into their houses and stole money and property.

Authorities imposed a 5 p.m.(1300 GMT) curfew and banned gatherings of more than two people on Anjouan, while two senior officials including the island's prefect were sacked for their refusal to implement orders from Moroni.
Anjouan island, about 130 km (80 miles) southeast of the main island of Grande Comore, is poorer than Grande Comore with few employment opportunities for its 190,000 population.
Military reinforcements arrived on Anjouan by air from the capital after being blocked at the airport on Thursday night by secessionists.
Anjouan residents started a general strike on Wednesday, setting up roadblocks, burning tyres and rejecting talks with the government.
The Comoro islands, which have had 17 coups and attempted coups since independence from France in 1975, have this year been swept by a series of strikes by civil servants demanding salary arrears.
